flashcard_questions.a: A quantity with magnitude only, and no direction.
A quantity with both magnitude and direction.

flashcard_questions.q: Which quantity is the vector version of speed?
In what unit is force measured?
What does a contact force require of the two objects?
Which force pushes upwards on an object floating in a fluid?
Which support force acts at right angles to a surface?
What is the gravitational field strength at the Earth's surface?
What is the gravitational field strength on the Moon?
What happens to your mass if you travel to the Moon?
What does a resultant force of zero tell you about an object?
flashcard_questions.a: It is stationary, or moving at constant speed in a straight line.

flashcard_questions.q: What does a resultant force that is not zero do to an object?
flashcard_questions.a: It accelerates in the direction of that resultant force.

flashcard_questions.q: (Higher) What does the length of an arrow on a free body diagram show?
flashcard_questions.a: The relative size of that force.

flashcard_questions.q: (Higher) Why does a falling skydiver reach terminal velocity?
flashcard_questions.a: Air resistance rises until it equals weight, so the resultant force is zero.
